text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Questions surround death of Turkish soldier and claims that the Greek Cypriot side was responsible. The Cyprus government speaks of Turkish provocations.
- Bomb was found close to the Turkish sentry post.
- The Foreign MInistry has made representations to Israel over flights in the Nicosia flight information region without informing the civil aviation department previously.
- Provocations. The occupying forces tried to implicate the Greek Cypriot side in an incident at one of their sentry posts in Vrysoulles.

- Jitters grip (centre right) Diko party after the declaration by its leader Spyros Kyprianou that he would run as candidate during elections in early 1998. Leading members describe the move premature.

- New serious crisis looms with serious consequences. The National Guard was not involved in death of Turkish Cypriot soldier, while Nicosia and Athens described the incident as a Turkish provocation.
- Shots which killed the Turkish Cypriot soldier came from the occupied areas.
- More than 60,000 elementary school students start school today.
- Turkish attempts fail to implicate the National Guard in the murder of a Turkish soldier and the wounding of another.
- (Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf) Denktash and Ankara are trying to sir up tension.
- Leading member of Diko party criticises leader for announcing he will be running for the presidency in 1998.
